text: Top leader proposes three major orientations to further promote APEC's role

SHENZHEN - General Secretary of the Communist Party of Việt Nam Central Committee and President Tô Lâm proposed three major orientations for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) to further promote its role amid profound changes in the global and regional landscape, at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday.
The top leader led a high-level Vietnamese delegation to the meeting, which was chaired by General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and President Xi Jinping.
In his remarks, he shared the country's vision and proposals for advancing APEC cooperation in a new era.

He noted that the Asia-Pacific is undergoing epoch-making transformations with both major opportunities and challenges, and stressed the urgent need to strengthen cooperation and connectivity among member economies to capitalise on opportunities and address shared challenges.

He affirmed that, emerging after a prolonged period of global division and conflict, APEC has become a symbol of efforts to heal divisions, build connections and promote dialogue and cooperation for shared prosperity.

Building on the principles of open regionalism, pioneering initiatives, a forward-looking development vision and the strong commitment of its 21 member economies, APEC has made significant contributions to the region's remarkable development.

Outlining the three major orientations for APEC, General Secretary and President Lâm said that first, APEC should take the lead in promoting an open trade and investment environment to create fresh momentum for economic integration and connectivity; ensuring smooth, stable and sustainable trade flows; maintaining the seamless operation of strategic supply chains; and strengthening the resilience, adaptability and self-reliance of individual economies and the region as a whole.
Second, APEC should open up new development spaces and create fresh growth drivers.
It should serve as an incubator for ideas and an optimal testing ground for next-generation institutional frameworks and growth models driven by technology and innovation.
It should also promote emerging economic models, including the digital, silver, care, low-altitude and 24/7 economies, to tap the region's full growth potential.
Third, APEC should promote dialogue and cooperation to build trust and maintain stability for development.
The forum should serve as an open, constructive channel for strategic dialogue and a bridge for parties to resolve differences, ease tensions and seek practical solutions.
Efforts to build consensus should be grounded in fairness, equality and mutually beneficial cooperation, and respecting one another's legitimate interests.
Leaders of APEC member economies highly valued General Secretary and President Lâm's remarks, particularly his proposed orientations for cooperation in the new period.

Under the theme 'Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together', the meeting discussed major trends in the global and regional economies, opportunities and challenges facing growth, trade and investment, and orientations for APEC cooperation in the coming period.
The leaders reaffirmed their strong commitment to building an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community for the prosperity of all people and future generations.
They agreed to continue efforts towards the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP), strengthen connectivity, facilitate trade and enhance supply chain resilience.

The meeting also highlighted the need to promote innovation- and productivity-driven growth, harness the potential of digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI), develop human resources and support small- and medium-sized enterprises.

Cooperation in addressing common challenges, ensuring energy and food security, and maintaining macro-economic stability was also emphasised, with a view to delivering tangible benefits to people and businesses.
At the conclusion of the meeting, the leaders adopted a Leaders' Declaration and three accompanying documents.

They praised the outcomes of APEC Year 2026 and expressed support and expectations for Việt Nam's hosting of APEC Year 2027, voicing confidence that it will generate fresh momentum for cooperation and contribute to peace, stability and shared prosperity across the Asia-Pacific region. - VNA/VNS
